what: Phillips 66 refines crude oil into fuels, owns midstream pipelines and processing plants, sells fuel under the Phillips 66, 76 and JET brands, and holds a half-share of the chemicals producer CPChem.
customers: Fuel distributors and branded service stations, airlines, chemicals buyers and energy shippers.
money: refineries in the US and Europe
pipelines, terminals and natural gas liquids processing
moat: Refineries connected to its own pipelines and terminals, so it captures margin at several points along the same barrel.
risks: Refining margins drive earnings and are outside its control
Revenue has fallen about 8% a year over three years
An activist investor has pressed for a breakup, creating strategic uncertainty
opportunities: Midstream earnings are contracted and cushion refining downturns
Buybacks and a dividend return most free cash flow
watch: Refining margin capture rate and midstream earnings growth.
